ready1_open_rewrite.title: SciVerse open question
ready1_open_rewrite.rewritten_question_text: Rainfall and biomass at several trophic levels in an ecosystem were measured over several years, and the results are shown in the figure below. Based on the results shown in the figure, this experiment indicates that environmental changes can affect which trophic levels in the ecosystem?
ready1_open_rewrite.expected_answer: All trophic levels of the ecosystem

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: Rainfall and biomass at several trophic levels in an ecosystem were measured over several years, and the results are shown in the figure below. Based on the results shown in the figure, this experiment indicates that environmental changes can affect which trophic levels in the ecosystem?
ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: All trophic levels of the ecosystem
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: The figure is a line graph titled “Rainfall and Biomass 2005–2011”. The horizontal axis is the years 2005 to 2011; the left vertical axis indicates rainfall, in inches; the right vertical axis indicates biomass. The legend shows that the gray line represents rainfall, the black solid line represents producers, and the black dotted line represents primary consumers. In the figure, rainfall is relatively high from 2005 to 2006, then decreases noticeably especially by 2008 and remains low. Producer biomass is relatively high around 2006, then also decreases greatly and remains at a low level. Primary consumer biomass likewise changes over time, and after rainfall decreases, it also drops to a lower level. Then reason: Rainfall is an environmental factor, and in the figure the biomass of two different trophic levels, producers and primary consumers, changes with rainfall. Producers and primary consumers belong to different trophic levels, indicating that the effect of environmental change is not limited to only one trophic level, but can affect all trophic levels through the ecosystem. Therefore, this experiment indicates that environmental changes can affect all trophic levels of the ecosystem.
